reason: The text, particularly in Exodus 18, explicitly presents and endorses a model of good leadership through organized government. Jethro advises Moses to delegate authority to 'men of strength, God-fearers, men of truth, haters of unjust gain' in a hierarchical structure of officers, specifically so they can judge the people efficiently. Jethro explicitly criticizes Moses' solo approach as 'not good' (לֹא־ טוֹב), warning it will exhaust both Moses and the people. The proposed governmental structure is designed to benefit the people by: providing accessible justice (all disputes can be addressed), avoiding burden and chaos, and enabling the people to come 'to their place in peace' (יָבֹא בְשָׁלוֹם). This directly exemplifies that good leadership is 'a functioning government to the benefit of the people.' The contrast with Pharaoh's oppressive rule further illustrates this principle negatively.
